Scope: Supported user-script facade and helpers in HL7Workbench.Scripting, API 2. Inherited .NET members and compiler-generated record equality, printing, copying and deconstruction use ordinary C# semantics; they are not host operations. Host transport/orchestration types are classified separately and are not supported authoring facilities. Public infrastructure types in the same referenced assembly can be named by trusted C#, but are unsupported host-orchestration facilities, not internal methods or a security boundary. Their exact metadata is included separately; it is excluded from facade completion and has no runnable authoring example.

InfrastructureTypes.ScriptDefinition: Host submission and API-version DTO, not a script entry point.
InfrastructureTypes.ScriptWorkerOptions: Parent process configuration; scripts cannot reconfigure their owning worker.
InfrastructureTypes.ScriptWorkerSession: Parent worker orchestration/transport, not a facade operation.

Entries.Title: Main / Complete and execution scopes
Entries.Description: Initialization runs once, Main once per captured selected message in logical input order, then optional Complete once after all Main calls succeed. Top-level variables persist within a run; each Run starts a fresh worker. Select Current message or Whole document in the editor. The host performs iteration; there is no document enumeration/navigation API in scripts.
Entries.Parameters: Main/Complete: no parameters. Scope is selected by the application, not changed from inside Main.
Entries.Returns: Both entry points return void. A successful run publishes a new independent unsaved output document.
Entries.Limitations: Exactly one top-level instance, synchronous, nongeneric, parameterless void Main and at most one matching Complete. No overloads, static/async/Task entries or background work. Failure skips Complete and discards staged output/reports. Never retain Message or ScriptSegment across invocations.

Entries.Title: Built-ins, My Scripts and starter examples
Entries.Signature: Duplicate Script → Rename Script → Save Script
Entries.Description: Built-in scripts are application-owned read-only entries. Duplicate Script saves an independent copy in My Scripts with a new ID. Rename and edit that copy, Save Script, reopen it and Run. Built-in updates do not rewrite user copies. Starter topics offer Create editable script, which creates an unsaved draft through the normal unsaved-change prompt.
Entries.Parameters: Use a descriptive local name (1–120 characters, no control characters). Choose Apply to scope before Run.
Entries.Returns: Saved user records keep their own stable identity and source. Ctrl+S in the script editor saves the script.
Entries.Limitations: Saving a script does not save HL7 output. Dirty drafts prompt before switching; failed saves keep the draft. Old development scripts require explicit rewrite/adoption. Duplicate Patient Deidentifier to configure its supported policy rather than creating another library preset.
